newsitem.title: UK: Clyde bid highlights oil firm value debate.
newsitem.headline: Clyde bid highlights oil firm value debate.

text.p: Gulf Canada's hostile bid for Clyde Petroleum Plc on Monday triggered a clash between different schools of thought on how to value oil exploration and production firms.

Clyde on Sunday dismissed the 432 million stg bid as too low on the basis of cash flow valuations, but Gulf Canada was backed by some analysts on Monday who said net asset value estimates suggested the offer was reasonable.
"Our view is certainly that it is a very good offer from Gulf," said one analyst, who declined to be named.
He said that the cash offer of 105 pence per share offers a fair premium over Clyde's net asset value, which he reckons is about 70 pence per share.
This analyst claimed the cash flow multiple approach as used by Clyde was too "crude" a method to value a production and exploration firm.
"Net asset value is far superior as it takes account of all the cash flow during the life (of existing reserves) and allows you to make all kinds of adjustments to it," he said.

Another industry watcher, however, favoured the cash multiple approach as he believed the net asset value method contained too many variables on such matters as oil price, tax and recovery rate to be of much use.

But he conceded that the cash flow methodology could be useful in analysing small firms, where production and exploration are much more transparent than with bigger firms like Enterprise Oil and LASMO Plc.
